title: Who buys from the incumbents
description: Reverse-engineered from the websites and press of ten traditional maritime security providers. These firms already hold the customer relationships we would be selling into. Only explicitly stated clients, customer types and partnerships are recorded; a logo we could not verify is not a client.

named_relationships.relationship: partnership to advance marine insurance and risk management
partnership covering threat and risk assessment, Gulf of Guinea guidance and optional 24-hour vessel tracking
named client, service contract 2019 to present

buyer_types.note: Named or described by eight of the ten providers researched.

buyer_types.buyer_type: Offshore, oil and gas, and subsea operators
buyer_types.note: Ambrey, Britannia, Castor Vali, Praesidium, ESC and Solace all state it. This segment is absent from our customer list.

buyer_types.buyer_type: Insurers, insurance and risk businesses, P&I stakeholders
buyer_types.note: Explicit partnerships or stated customer type, not an inference that the insurer bought guarding.
Includes the one hard-named client in the whole sweep, EUCAP.

scale_benchmarks.note: Two figures published: 35 average, and 25-30 for the Indian Ocean Region and West Africa.

scale_benchmarks.claim: approved to provide armed security on more than 40 flag states' vessels

scale_benchmarks.note: The clearest statement anywhere in this sweep that the largest ship managers buy this service.

scale_benchmarks.claim: one fleet contract maintained for four years
scale_benchmarks.note: From a testimonial; the client is not named.

gatekeepers.finding: The incumbents route through insurance. Ambrey partners with Insurwave, MAST with Beazley, Praesidium carries Lloyd's policies, and ESC states it is vetted by flag states, ship managers and P&I clubs. Vetting by a P&I club appears to be a precondition of selling, not a nice-to-have.
gatekeepers.implication_for_us: P&I clubs and war risk underwriters are not buyers, but they are the gate. Our gtm.json listed them only under do-not-target; on this evidence they belong in the plan as a channel and an accreditation step.

gaps: Almost no end customer is named anywhere. Nine of ten providers name no shipowner client at all. The industry does not publish its customer list.
The only hard-named client in the sweep is a government mission, EUCAP, not a commercial shipowner.
Neptune P2P Group returned nothing; no usable source was located.
Offshore energy appears in six of ten provider client lists and is completely absent from our customer research.
No pricing is published by any provider.
scope_note: Five of ten incumbents serve governments and defence, and two serve NGOs. Those buyer types are out of scope for us and are recorded only to explain the incumbents' revenue mix, not as targets.
